# Sysadmin agent tools

The `sysadmin` agent (`sysadmin_agent`) publishes 10 tools to the [Tool Registry](../TOOL_REGISTRY.md). This page is generated from the agent's code: names, descriptions and parameters come from the tool definitions, action classes from `audit.ToolClassification`, and capabilities and eligibility from the agent card options. Capability names are defined in the [capability vocabulary](capabilities.md).

| Tool | Action class | Capabilities |
|---|---|---|
| [`check_disk`](#check_disk) | read | `host_disk` |
| [`check_host`](#check_host) | read | `process_status` |
| [`check_memory`](#check_memory) | read | `host_memory` |
| [`get_host_logs`](#get_host_logs) | read | `logs` |
| [`get_pgbackrest_status`](#get_pgbackrest_status) | read | `backup_status` |
| [`read_pg_log_file`](#read_pg_log_file) | read | `logs` |
| [`restart_container`](#restart_container) | destructive | `process_restart` |
| [`restart_service`](#restart_service) | destructive | `process_restart` |
| [`restore_from_backup`](#restore_from_backup) | destructive | `data_restore` |
| [`run_pgbackrest_backup`](#run_pgbackrest_backup) | write | `backup_run` |

## `check_disk`

Show disk utilization on the host (df -h). Use to determine whether the database stopped due to a full data or log volume.

- **Action class:** read
- **Capabilities:** `host_disk`
- **Fleet eligible:** no
- **Auto-remediation eligible:** no

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `run_on_host` | boolean | no | If true, run df on the VM host OS instead of inside the container. Ignored for systemd targets. |
| `target` | string | no | Server ID from infrastructure config. When omitted, runs df on the agent host. |

## `check_host`

Check the status of the database process on the host. For Docker/Podman targets, inspects the container state. For systemd targets, shows the service ActiveState and SubState.

- **Action class:** read
- **Capabilities:** `process_status`
- **Fleet eligible:** no
- **Auto-remediation eligible:** no
- **Example prompts:** "Is the alloydb-omni container running?"

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | string | yes | required,Server ID from infrastructure config (e.g. 'prod_db'), or a connection string / port (e.g. 'host=127.0.0.1 port=5432' or '5432') when the server ID is unknown — resolved by port matching. |

## `check_memory`

Show memory utilization on the host (free -h). Use to detect OOM conditions that may have caused the database process to be killed.

- **Action class:** read
- **Capabilities:** `host_memory`
- **Fleet eligible:** no
- **Auto-remediation eligible:** no

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `run_on_host` | boolean | no | If true, run free on the VM host OS instead of inside the container. Ignored for systemd targets. |
| `target` | string | no | Server ID from infrastructure config. When omitted, runs free on the agent host. |

## `get_host_logs`

Retrieve recent log lines from the database process. For Docker/Podman uses 'docker/podman logs'. For systemd uses journalctl. Use when the DB is down and read_pg_log is unavailable.

- **Action class:** read
- **Capabilities:** `logs`
- **Fleet eligible:** no
- **Auto-remediation eligible:** no
- **Example prompts:** "Show the last 200 log lines from the prod_db container"

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | string | yes | required,Server ID from infrastructure config, or a connection string / port — resolved by port matching. |
| `filter` | string | no | Optional substring to filter log lines (case-sensitive). |
| `lines` | integer | no | Number of recent log lines to return (default 100). |

## `get_pgbackrest_status`

Check pgBackRest backup-job health: stanza status, the most recent backup's label/time/type, and whether it's stale relative to the expected schedule. This is the backup-taking precondition — distinct from the database agent's get_backup_status, which checks WAL archiving health via pg_stat_archiver.

- **Action class:** read
- **Capabilities:** `backup_status`
- **Fleet eligible:** no
- **Auto-remediation eligible:** no
- **Example prompts:** "Check whether pgBackRest's last backup for prod_db is stale"

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max_age_hours` | integer | no | How many hours old the most recent successful backup may be before it's considered stale. Default 25 (one day plus margin) — override to match the target's actual backup schedule. Zero or negative values fall back to the default; there is no way to force an immediate backup to read as stale via this parameter. |
| `stanza` | string | no | pgBackRest stanza name. When omitted, the only stanza present is used — an error if more than one exists. |
| `target` | string | no | Server ID from infrastructure config. Required whenever infrastructure config is loaded — omitting it then is treated as a resolution failure and errors loudly, not a request to run locally. Only leave this empty when no infrastructure config exists at all (a genuinely colocated deployment). If your connection_string/server ID doesn't match a known infrastructure entry, do not guess or omit target — report that as its own finding and escalate. |

## `read_pg_log_file`

Read the PostgreSQL log file directly from inside the container or pod (via exec). Works when Postgres is down — does not require a live database connection. Use get_host_logs for process stdout/stderr; use this tool for the PostgreSQL log file written by logging_collector.

- **Action class:** read
- **Capabilities:** `logs`
- **Fleet eligible:** no
- **Auto-remediation eligible:** no

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | string | yes | required,Server ID from infrastructure config. |
| `filter` | string | no | Only return lines containing this string (case-insensitive). Useful for: ERROR, FATAL, PANIC, OOM, 'no space'. |
| `lines` | integer | no | Number of recent log lines to return (default 100). |
| `log_path` | string | no | Override the log directory path inside the container. Default: /var/lib/postgresql/data/log. |

## `restart_container`

Restart a Docker or Podman container hosting the database. Requires the server to have a container_runtime and container_name configured in infrastructure.json. Use restart_service for systemd-managed databases.

- **Action class:** destructive
- **Capabilities:** `process_restart`
- **Fleet eligible:** no
- **Auto-remediation eligible:** yes
- **Example prompts:** "Restart the prod_db container — crash loop detected"

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reason` | string | yes | required,Human-readable reason for the restart. Logged for audit trail. |
| `target` | string | yes | required,Server ID from infrastructure config, or a connection string / port — resolved by port matching. |

## `restart_service`

Restart a systemd service hosting the database (systemctl restart). Requires the server to have a systemd_unit configured in infrastructure.json. Use restart_container for Docker/Podman-managed databases.

- **Action class:** destructive
- **Capabilities:** `process_restart`
- **Fleet eligible:** no
- **Auto-remediation eligible:** yes

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reason` | string | yes | required,Human-readable reason for the restart. Logged for audit trail. |
| `target` | string | yes | required,Server ID from infrastructure config, or a connection string / port — resolved by port matching. |

## `restore_from_backup`

Restore the database from the latest pgBackRest backup, overwriting the current data directory (destructive — requires operator approval). Restore-to-latest only: no point-in-time target. Refuses outright if the server is still accepting connections (pg_isready). Use only when get_pgbackrest_status confirms a healthy, non-stale backup exists and the instance is confirmed down — never against a broken repo/stanza or a live instance.

- **Action class:** destructive
- **Capabilities:** `data_restore`
- **Fleet eligible:** no
- **Auto-remediation eligible:** no

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `stanza` | string | no | pgBackRest stanza name. When omitted, the only stanza present is used — an error if more than one exists. |
| `target` | string | no | Server ID from infrastructure config. Required whenever infrastructure config is loaded — omitting it then is treated as a resolution failure and errors loudly, not a request to run locally. Only leave this empty when no infrastructure config exists at all (a genuinely colocated deployment). If your connection_string/server ID doesn't match a known infrastructure entry, do not guess or omit target — report that as its own finding and escalate. |

## `run_pgbackrest_backup`

Take a fresh pgBackRest backup (default type=full). Requires operator approval (Write action). Use only to remediate a STALE backup on an otherwise-healthy repo (get_pgbackrest_status status_code=0, backup_stale=true) — never against a broken repo/stanza (status_code != 0), which needs human investigation, not a new backup attempt.

- **Action class:** write
- **Capabilities:** `backup_run`
- **Fleet eligible:** no
- **Auto-remediation eligible:** no

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `stanza` | string | no | pgBackRest stanza name. When omitted, the only stanza present is used — an error if more than one exists. |
| `target` | string | no | Server ID from infrastructure config. Required whenever infrastructure config is loaded — omitting it then is treated as a resolution failure and errors loudly, not a request to run locally. Only leave this empty when no infrastructure config exists at all (a genuinely colocated deployment). If your connection_string/server ID doesn't match a known infrastructure entry, do not guess or omit target — report that as its own finding and escalate. |
| `type` | string | no | Backup type: full, diff, or incr. Default full — always valid regardless of backup history, unlike diff/incr which require a prior full backup to reference. |
